events.name: Badminton at the 2026 Asian Games - Team Event
events.coverage: India's men's and women's team-event matches. Singapore did not enter the team event.

sources.label: Badminton at the 2026 Asian Games (Wikipedia)
Badminton at the 2026 Asian Games - Men's team (Wikipedia)
Badminton at the 2026 Asian Games - Women's team (Wikipedia)

events.notes: Level set to MAJOR by analogy with the Olympics/World Championships tier in rules.json; the Asian Games isn't a BWF Tour event so it has no official tier name of its own. Team entries (MT/WT) replace the earlier per-discipline entries; rubbers are recorded inside each tie, not as separate entries. Men's team: India beat Bangladesh (R16) and Japan (QF), lost to China (SF) and won bronze; per this bracket format (byes=yes, no third-place match shown) semifinal losers are awarded bronze directly. Women's team: India beat Kazakhstan (R16), lost to Japan (QF) and were eliminated without a medal (only semifinal losers medal in this format). Neither bracket used a group stage; both were straight knockout with byes for the top 4 seeds, so no G1/G2/G3 ties apply this edition. Un-played rubbers after a tie was already decided are marked NOT_PLAYED, matching the 'np' cells on the source scoreboards. Singapore did not enter either squad list, confirming the team event has no Singaporean entries.

events.name: China Smash 2026
events.coverage: India and Singapore entries in qualifying and the main draw. All qualifiers were eliminated before the main draw. In the main draw, direct entries and wild cards from both countries are in singles, doubles and mixed doubles; some results are in and some matches are still to be played.

sources.label: China Smash 2026 (Wikipedia)
China Smash 2026 - Qualification (Wikipedia)

events.notes: Qualifying (1-3 Oct) eliminated every IND/SGP qualifier, including Diya Chitale's close Q2 loss to Zhu Chengzhu (HKG), so none reached the main draw via qualifying. Several IND/SGP players entered the main draw directly as seeds/wild cards (not through qualifying): Manush Shah, Manav Thakkar, Manika Batra and Sreeja Akula (IND); Izaac Quek, Ser Lin Qian and Zeng Jian (SGP) in singles, plus doubles/mixed doubles pairs. The main draw bracket page does not give per-match dates/times, only round-by-round day ranges, so SCHEDULED matches are left without a date. Xiaona Shan (GER) / Zeng Jian (SGP) is a cross-country pairing in women's doubles per the official draw; recorded under SGP since that is the tracked country. Manav Thakkar/Manush Shah (IND) and Izaac Quek/Koen Pang (SGP) in men's doubles, and Diya Chitale/Yashaswini Ghorpade (IND) in women's doubles, still have byes into the second round but their opponent is not yet decided (the other half of their section has not played), so no next match is recorded for them yet. Manav Thakkar's (IND) R64 match vs Simon Gauzy (FRA) is left SCHEDULED: the Wikipedia bracket's own per-game scores for that match (9-11, 9-11, 11-7, 11-5, 12-10) add up to a 3-2 win for Thakkar, but the page bolds Gauzy as the match winner and lists Gauzy, not Thakkar, in the next round slot. That is an internal contradiction on the source page itself; rather than guess which side is the transcription error, this match is left unrecorded until the page is corrected or a second source confirms the result.
